title: Causes of the First World War Knowledge Base
topic: History - Causes of World War One
summary: Comprehensive atomic breakdown of the long-term causes (Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, Nationalism), the trigger event, the July Crisis escalation timeline, and major historical interpretations surrounding the outbreak of World War One.

knowledge.text: MAIN is the acronym for the four long-term causes of the First World War: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, and Nationalism.
Militarism before World War One manifested as an arms race, particularly the Anglo-German naval race.
The Dreadnought battleship was launched in 1906.
The Schlieffen Plan was Germany's military plan to attack France by invading through neutral Belgium.
The Triple Alliance was formed between Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy.
The Triple Entente was formed between Britain, France, and Russia.
The alliance system posed the danger of escalating a local conflict into a general European war.
Imperialism created friction among European powers through intense rivalry for overseas colonies.
The Moroccan Crises took place in 1905 and 1911.
Nationalist tensions prior to 1914 included Slav nationalism in the Balkans and Serbian expansionist ambitions.
France harboured nationalist desire to regain Alsace-Lorraine, which had been lost to Germany in 1871.
Archduke Franz Ferdinand was assassinated on 28 June 1914 in Sarajevo.
Archduke Franz Ferdinand was assassinated by Gavrilo Princip.
Gavrilo Princip was a member of the Black Hand, a Serbian nationalist group.
Germany issued the 'blank cheque' of unconditional support to Austria-Hungary on 5-6 July 1914.
Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia on 23 July 1914.
Austria declared war on Serbia on 28 July 1914.
In response to Austria's declaration of war on Serbia, Russia mobilised its armed forces.
Germany declared war on Russia on 1 August 1914.
Germany declared war on France on 3 August 1914.
Germany invaded Belgium as part of its strategic offensive.
Britain declared war on Germany on 4 August 1914.
Britain justified entering the war by citing the 1839 Treaty of London, which guaranteed Belgian neutrality.
The Fischer thesis (1961) argues that Germany bore the main responsibility for World War One because it deliberately sought expansion.
Christopher Clark (2012) argues for shared responsibility among powers, putting forward the thesis that European nations were 'sleepwalking' into war.
Article 231 of the Treaty of Versailles was known as the 'war guilt clause' and placed sole blame for the war on Germany.

intro.text: Militarism, alliances, imperialism, and nationalism set the stage for World War One.
An arms race and rival alliance blocs made Europe a ticking time bomb.
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand triggered the July Crisis in 1914.
Blank cheques, ultimatums, and mobilization quickly cascaded into a continent-wide war.
Germany declared war on France on 3 August 1914.

sequence.title: Road to War 1914
sequence.instructions: Follow the chain of events that led to global conflict.

steps.label: Alsace-Lorraine Loss
steps.detail: In 1871, France lost Alsace-Lorraine to Germany, fuelling a nationalist desire to regain it.

steps.label: First Moroccan Crisis
steps.detail: In 1905, rivalry for colonies flared over Morocco (a second crisis followed in 1911).

steps.label: Dreadnought Launch
steps.detail: The Dreadnought battleship was launched in 1906, accelerating the naval arms race.

steps.label: Assassination in Sarajevo
steps.detail: Archduke Franz Ferdinand was assassinated on 28 June 1914 by Gavrilo Princip.

steps.label: The Blank Cheque
steps.detail: Germany issued unconditional support to Austria-Hungary on 5-6 July 1914.

steps.label: Ultimatum Issued
steps.detail: Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia on 23 July 1914.

steps.label: War Declared on Serbia
steps.detail: Austria declared war on Serbia on 28 July 1914, prompting Russian mobilization.

steps.label: Schlieffen Plan Activation
steps.detail: In August 1914, Germany invaded neutral Belgium to attack France, bringing Britain into the war.

arena.title: Long-term vs July Crisis
arena.instructions: Shoot items belonging to the Long-term causes category and let others pass.

clues.label: Fischer Book
clues.claim: Germany bore main responsibility for the war.
clues.why: The Fischer thesis argues Germany deliberately sought expansion.

clues.label: Sleepwalker Clock
clues.claim: Powers sleepwalked into war with shared responsibility.
clues.why: Christopher Clark argues for shared responsibility and sleepwalking.

clues.label: Article 231
clues.claim: Placed sole blame for the war strictly on Germany.
clues.why: Article 231 of the Treaty of Versailles is known as the war guilt clause.

clues.label: Escalation Danger
clues.claim: The alliance system risked turning local conflicts general.
clues.why: The alliance system posed the clear danger of escalating conflicts.
